questions.key_step: Put $t=2x+3y$; then a separable equation with a partial-fraction integral and matching of constants.
questions.justification: Routine substitution, one partial fraction, constant matching; numerical answer.

questions.key_step: Shift the origin to $(1,1)$, then the homogeneous substitution $Y=tX$.
questions.justification: Standard shift plus homogeneous DE, integral of $\frac{1-t}{1+t^2}$ and reading $\alpha,\beta$ from the given form; no insight beyond coaching routine.

questions.key_step: Separate variables; $\int\frac{1+\ln x}{x}dx$ and $\tan(\frac\pi4-\theta)$.
questions.justification: Direct separable DE; the only care is the tangent subtraction formula to match the form.

questions.key_step: L'Hopital in $r$ gives $f^2=xff'-x^3e^{f/x}$, then $y=vx$.
questions.justification: Limit manipulation hidden inside a functional definition, then a homogeneous DE with $\int ve^{-v}dv$; several stages and an unusual set-up.

questions.key_step: Tangent intercepts and area give $-x^2y'+2xy=2$; solve the linear equation.
questions.justification: Modelling step (intercepts, area) before a routine linear DE; sign care needed, numerical answer.

questions.key_step: $t=\tan x$, $u=1/t$ turns a Bernoulli-type equation into a linear one in $y$.
questions.justification: Two chained substitutions to reach a linear equation with exponentials; less familiar than a plain linear DE.

questions.key_step: Linear in $x$ with I.F. $(t+1)^{-2}$.
questions.justification: One familiar move (I.F.) and a polynomial integral; numerical.

questions.key_step: Treat $x$ as the dependent variable; I.F. $\frac1y$.
questions.justification: One familiar move applied once; options absent but the arithmetic is short.

questions.key_step: $|x-y|\le y\iff0\le x\le2y$; integrate parabola minus line.
questions.justification: Decoding the modulus region then a routine area; options help.

questions.key_step: Tangent from $A(-2,0)$: $m=\frac14$, $B(6,2)$; area by $dy$ strips.
questions.justification: Tangent condition then a short area; two routine stages with options.

questions.key_step: Intersections $x=-6,4$; parabola minus line.
questions.justification: One standard area integral between a parabola and a line.

questions.key_step: Upper boundary switches at $x=1$; split the integral.
questions.justification: Min of two lines over a parabola, two integrals; routine but with more bookkeeping.

questions.key_step: Chord $x=2\sqrt3$ is the diameter; half-disc minus parabola area.
questions.justification: Circle-parabola intersection and a half-disc/parabola split; routine with a sketch.

questions.key_step: $f=e^{4ax}$, the DE fixes $a=\frac12$, then $\int_0^2e^xdx$.
questions.justification: Functional equation to exponential, characteristic equation, then a trivial area; short chain of standard steps.

questions.key_step: Shift by $2$; area between $X^2=Y$ and $Y^2=-8X$.
questions.justification: Standard pair of parabolas after one shift; formula or direct integral.

questions.key_step: For $x<0$ the integrand is $a$; split at $0$ and solve for $a$.
questions.justification: Modulus-exponential boundary split, integrate, solve linear equation in $a$.

questions.key_step: Rectangle with corner $(t,t)$ on $y=x$ and top on the parabola; maximise.
questions.justification: Modelling the inscribed rectangle correctly (which edge is binding) then calculus with an awkward fraction; precision and set-up risk.

questions.key_step: Shift to $y=x^2-2$ vs $y=|x|$; use symmetry.
questions.justification: Completing the square and handling $|x+2|$ by shift/symmetry; routine.

questions.key_step: For $x<0$, $|e^x-1|=1-e^x$; meet at $e^x=\frac12$.
questions.justification: Modulus of an exponential then one integral; routine.

questions.key_step: Top boundary is $\min(2|x|+1,x^2+1)$; symmetric, split at $2$.
questions.justification: Min of line and parabola with symmetry; two short integrals.
